tagline: An Olmsted parkway along the Providence River.
intro: From Second Street near the Washington Bridge the parkway climbs around Fort Hill and follows the escarpment above the Providence River, with the city and the port across the water. Then it leaves the river, drops to a causeway over Watchemoket Cove and rises again past Squantum Woods to Pawtucket Avenue, 2.4 miles in all.

Designed by the Olmsted firm and tied to the Greater Metropolitan Park Plan for Providence, it was built between 1910 and 1920. Old maples, oaks, black pines and sycamores line it, and along the northern stretch the East Bay Bike Path keeps it company on the river side.

moments.title: Fort Hill Overlook
moments.text: The overlook at the top of the hill faces the Providence skyline across the river, and across the road is the site of a fort built in 1775 against the British.

moments.title: Watchemoket Cove
moments.text: Where the parkway crosses the cove on its causeway and bridge, an informal parking area by the pumping station gave a view of the water and its birds, according to the 1999 stewardship plan.

moments.title: Squantum Point
moments.text: Providence merchants and sea captains used to row out to a small island off the point for clambakes, and when its owner objected, local men bought the point itself in 1870.

sources.label: RIDOT, Veterans Memorial Parkway Stewardship Plan (1999), pages 1 to 6
